## Clockwork Brain Gear (CR 3)

**XP** 800  
 N(E) Small construct  
 **Init** +0; **Senses** darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +9  

**Defense**

 **AC** 10, touch 6, flat-footed 10 (–5 Dex, +4 natural, +1 size)  
 **hp** 42 (5d10+10 plus 5)  
 Fort +3; Ref—4; **Will** +7  
 **Defensive Abilities** hardness 10; **Immune** construct traits  
 **Weaknesses** immobile  

**Offense**

 **Speed** 0 ft.  
 **Space** 5 ft.; **Reach** 0 ft.  

**Statistics**

 **Str** 10, Dex—, Con—, **Int** 20, **Wis** 18, **Cha** 14  
 **Base Atk** +5; **CMB** +4; **CMD** 9 (can’t be tripped)  
 **Feats** Great Fortitude, Iron Will, Toughness  
 **Skills** Diplomacy +7, Craft (metalworking) +10, Knowledge (arcana) +10, Knowledge (engineering) +10, Perception +9, Sense Motive +9, Spellcraft +10  
 **SQ** control clockworks, dream  

**Special Abilities**

 **Control Clockwork (Su)** Any clockwork that comes within two miles of a brain gear immediately falls under that brain gear’s control. If more than one brain gear attempts to control a clockwork (or if the clockwork is under the control of another brain gear or overseer), each gear must make an opposed Intelligence check; the winner gains control of that clockwork. When a clockwork moves more than 2 miles away from a brain gear, it continues to perform the last order given to it, but there is a 25% percent chance each hour that it ceases to function, collapsing into a pile of junk. If a brain gear later moves within two miles of the destroyed clockwork, the clockwork can reactivate if it has the self-repair ability. Otherwise, it remains destroyed.
